page: Microsoft Azure M32ls_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MSMediumMemoryv4 family. Powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware profile does not include graphics accelerators, focusing compute resources entirely on general CPU and memory operations.

The instance does not feature bundled local ephemeral storage, meaning all persistent and scratch volumes must be hosted via external Premium Storage interfaces. While this architecture decouples persistence from physical host life cycles, it shifts disk I/O performance to remote network-attached block storage rather than local NVMe drives.

Given the dense 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio, the M32ls_v4 targets memory capacity over high thread counts. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for systems constrained primarily by RAM capacity, making it appropriate for large in-memory caching solutions, enterprise relational database management systems, and transactional workloads.

Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the architecture delivers a memory-to-core density of 16.0 GB per vCPU, specifically targeting applications with large memory footprints. The configuration includes zero GPUs and provides no local physical storage, requiring attached Premium Storage disks for operating system and data requirements. By decoupling compute and storage resources, the instance enables flexible volume management without tying persistent data to the physical host lifecycle. The high memory ratio makes M32ls_v4 well suited for enterprise database engines, in-memory caches, distributed analytics nodes, and transactional workloads demanding extensive memory capacity alongside moderate multi-threaded compute.
